hints: Notice the question asks for the one combination that does not give total charge zero or $+1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, which is $+1e$.
Recall the quark charges in units of $e$: up is $+2/3e$, while down and strange are each $-1/3e$.
Add the three fractional charges for each option and compare the sum to $0$ and to $+1$ to find the one that gives $+2$.
walkthrough: Recall the quark charges: up quark $= +2/3e$, down quark $= -1/3e$, strange quark $= -1/3e$, where $e = +1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
Add charges for each three-quark combination as fractions of $e$.
For up, down, down: $+2/3 -1/3 -1/3 = 0$, so charge $0$. For up, strange, strange: $+2/3 -1/3 -1/3 = 0$, so charge $0$.
Only the $+2e$ result is neither zero nor $+1e$. This is option D.

options.A: Total charge is $+2/3e -1/3e -1/3e = 0$, so it gives a neutral particle and is allowed.
options.B: Strange quark has charge $-1/3e$ like down, so total is $+2/3e -1/3e -1/3e = 0$, a neutral particle.
options.C: Total charge is $+2/3e +2/3e -1/3e = +1e$, which is $+1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and is allowed.
options.D: Total charge is $+2/3e +2/3e +2/3e = +2e$, which is $+3.2 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, neither zero nor $+1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
